content:
sarah-sales: Hey team — ACME POC is blocked. Their client POSTs a ~13MB JSON blob (lots of base64 attachments + long HTML) and our API returns 413 Request Entity Too Large. Demo scheduled tomorrow, they need a quick unblock. cc @jordan-se

jordan-se: Can you paste the exact curl they use and the response headers/body?

sarah-sales: Sure — customer pasted this:``` 
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d @payload.json
```
Response: `HTTP/1.1 413 Request Entity Too Large` + empty body. payload.json is ~13.2MB, JSON with `context` field containing base64 images + full-page HTML.

jordan-se: Yup that's hitting our request body limit. Quick options: 1) Have them upload the large context to an object store and call us with a pointer (context_url) — we can fetch it server-side. 2) Ask them to gzip the payload and set `Content-Encoding: gzip` (we accept gzipped bodies up to a higher limit). 3) Strip large binaries and attach them separately via presign / upload. Which is least friction for ACME? :thinking:

sarah-sales: They said they can't open an S3 bucket on their side, but they can hit a single presigned URL we provide. They don't want to change the client much. Also worried about security scanning of gzipped payloads.

mike-ops: We have an internal presign helper we can enable per-account for POCs. We can issue a one-time presign for ACME and set TTL=1h and private ACL. @ops-bot can you create it and add it to the acme-poc account?

ops-bot: Presign job created: `presign-789abc` (TTL=3600s). Endpoint: `https://internal.presign.redwood/acme/presign/789abc` — added to `acme-poc` account. Audit log entry generated.

jordan-se: Suggested workflow to send to ACME: 1) PUT the gzipped JSONL to the presign URL. 2) Call the infer endpoint with a small JSON body that references the URL, e.g.:```
POST /v1/infer
{
  "model": "rwd-ggml-1b",
  "context_url": "https://internal.presign.redwood/acme/presign/789abc?signature=...",
  "context_type": "jsonl-gz",
  "max_tokens": 512
}
```
Server will fetch, decompress, and tokenize server-side. This avoids client body size limits. Note: we still tokenize the content and it counts toward usage.

sarah-sales: Thanks. They asked a billing question: if we fetch the context from a URL, are those tokens billable? Also they asked if the presign URL outbound fetch keeps data in-region (they require EU only).

prithvi-pm: Yes — any context we fetch and tokenize counts toward hosted usage. For this POC I can approve a 1M-token credit so they don't get charged. Regarding regions: presign URLs can be served from regional fetchers; I've enabled `eu-west-1` for the acme account. We'll record this in the security checklist: private presign, 1hr TTL, audit logs.

sarah-sales: Perfect — I'll forward instructions + the presign link. I'll also include the curl example and mention the billing credit. If they still see 413 we'll try chunked uploads/streaming. Meeting in 45 to sync.

jordan-se: One more ops note: if they replay many large contexts quickly, it can trip our tokenization concurrency quota. Recommend pacing to ~1 request/sec until we confirm capacity. Also avoid extremely long max_tokens on the initial ingest.

sarah-sales: Got it, thanks :thumbsup:
